item.title: Looking Back
item.description: But soon this drifting period will pass and I will again embrace the life I’ve been given, with a loving family and friends and a still-functioning brain.

item.title: Managing Body and Environmental Temperature Swings in Kids with Paralysis
item.description: Any disease or injury to the nervous system can result in a child’s inability to internally control their body temperature. This is called thermodysregulation.

item.title: How SCI Reshaped My Family
item.description: The injury did not steal our family; it redirected it toward more intentional care, clearer communication, and a steady, patient love that can hold up under pressure.

item.title: Peer & Family Support Program Spotlight: Nathaniel Clark
item.description: “At a basic level, it made me realize what was possible,” he says. “They let me know that resources are out there. That the trail had already been blazed, and there are avenues for assistance, if you want it.”

item.title: Caring For Those Who Care For Us
item.description: Relationships are full of joy, fun, and love. But they are work, too, especially when one person needs the other to be their caregiver every day.

item.title: Adapting and Growing As We Age
item.description: Each time we struggle against a new obstacle, it can make us stronger, more resilient, better able to adapt to future challenges, which in turn creates confidence, hope, and more ways to appreciate life than we ever thought possible.

item.title: Parenting Teenagers and Holding on for Dear Life
item.description: When I met Geoff, despite his spinal cord injury and paralysis, I knew he would make a great father.

item.title: Quality of Life Grantee Spotlight: Chicago No Limits Fishing
item.description: In 2025, CNLF received a $24,999 Quality of Life grant to purchase a larger, fully accessible three-pontoon boat that would more than double passenger capacity.

item.title: Quality of Life Grantee Spotlight: AccesSurf Hawai’i
item.description: In 2025, ASH received a $24,000 Christopher & Dana Reeve Foundation Quality of Life Grant to expand the frequency of their swim clinic from quarterly to monthly.

item.title: Cómo controlar los cambios de temperatura corporales y ambientales en niños con parálisis
item.description: En el cerebro, el hipotálamo controla la temperatura corporal a través del sistema nervioso autónomo.
